reasons.issue: Illegal penalty-kill roster: only 2 Navy skaters (YOU, D1) were shown against 5 Gold skaters. A team can never be reduced below 3 skaters on major hockey rulebooks (NHL/Hockey Canada/USA Hockey all cap simultaneous minors at two, i.e. 5-on-3 is the maximum shorthanded disadvantage); 5-on-2 does not occur in real play, and the sibling scene exp26-u15-003 in packet-31.json (same age band and family) shows a validated 4-on-5 kill with actors F1(-16,5,f~1.95) and F2(-15,-3,f~1.80) on the HOME team -- positions matching this scene's F1/F2 almost to the decimal, but tagged team:'away' here.
reasons.change: Restored F1 and F2 to team:'home' (now h3/h4) and added two more Navy skaters (F3, D2) to reach a legal 4-on-5 kill. Briefing now states the ratio explicitly ('five skaters against four'), matching the cited source's own framing ('whether you have four on the kill or you have five on the power play').

sourceChecks.scope: Read the full interview (fetched with a browser user-agent after a plain WebFetch 403). Guentzel discusses faceoff preparation ('a key is the faceoff -- having everybody on the same page, whether you have four on the kill or you have five on the power play... get a puck out on the penalty kill'), PK pressure/coverage mindset ('if you're down a man, you really have to work together to minimize your deficiencies'; 'stepping up on the half-boards'), and general special-teams structure. This supports the stated coaching principles in both scenarios (numeric framing of 4-on-the-kill / 5-on-the-power-play, PK coverage/pressure, faceoff-then-retrieval mindset) at a general level; it does not certify these exact coordinates, this exact 'flank-to-flank shift' terminology, or any guaranteed outcome. Editor's note on the same page: 'USA Hockey strongly recommends refraining from detailed and lengthy instructing on special teams tactics/systems until the 14U age classification at the earliest' -- both scenarios are ageBand U15 (Bantam-equivalent), at/above that threshold, supporting the age check.
sourceChecks.ageFormat: General/14U+ (source's own age floor for special-teams systems instruction); scenarios use Canadian-style 'U15' banding, the same Bantam-age cohort.
